title: The suggested donation
hook: Does changing suggested amounts change your chosen gift?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish a donation suggestion from a minimum requirement and inspect the response distribution.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish a donation suggestion from a minimum requirement and inspect the response distribution.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A campaign suggests €20 but sets no minimum. In this toy rule, is a €5 gift allowed? Toy inputs A=[20, 5, 0]; B=[20, 5, 20].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[5, 0, 5], [5, 20, 0]]. Labels: Gift €, Minimum €, Above min €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: A suggested amount and a minimum are different constraints. A recommendation can influence attention while still leaving smaller gifts feasible; introducing an actual minimum changes the available choices.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Suggested €=20, Gift €=5, Minimum €=20. What is Gift €? Answer: 5.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Suggested €=20, Gift €=5, Minimum €=20. What is Gift €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 5. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Suggested amounts in fundraising pull donations toward them (Edwards & List, 2014).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish a donation suggestion from a minimum requirement and inspect the response distribution.
